Without initiation there is no eligibility for Shaiva yoga. And initiation does not bring about only eligibility for yoga.

tokens.grounds: identifies the true initiation in this case

quick_english: Then knowledge itself is initiation, as explained in the revered Traisika. And for him there suddenly arises knowledge of the meaning of all the scriptures.

tokens.grounds: states the effect of the teaching

quick_english: Seeking benefit for himself or for others, he should contemplate this. By that statement in the Malini scripture, all of this has been made clear.

tokens.grounds: describes how the goal is reached

quick_english: Because inclinations differ, attainment of the goal is impelled by mantra. In the offering, mantra, seal, path, and substances have a common use.
Because inclinations differ, the fruits of disciples and of the teacher differ. The Shaiva practitioner is twofold: one whose way of life abandons worldly concerns.
One type follows worldly duty, desires fruit, abides in what is good, and avoids what is evil. The seeker of liberation is twofold: the seedless one is free from pledges and the like.

tokens.grounds: describes the other type of candidate

quick_english: Another kind of candidate is like a child, a fool, an old person, a woman, an enjoyer, or someone sick. For such a person, the teaching of Shiva prescribes the seeded initiation.

tokens.grounds: assigns the obligation to that group

quick_english: But for those who can endure the pairs of opposites, there is a seeded initiation made of pledges that confers grace. They must observe it, and they must also keep the special pledges.

tokens.grounds: states what is not to be done

quick_english: For a desireless seeker of liberation, one should clearly contemplate the non-existence of past and future actions. But one should not do anything to remove the action that has already begun.

tokens.grounds: contrasts with the seeker of liberation

tokens.grounds: names what is not purified away

When the body formed by already-begun karma falls away, this person enjoys powers such as aṇimā. After enjoying them, he goes onward to the level where he becomes joined, whether in the sakala state or in a limited condition.

tokens.grounds: explains why it gives immediate liberation

quick_english: This seedless initiation is said to give immediate liberation, because it cuts away the three bonds of past, future, and already-begun karma.

tokens.grounds: states the problem in the seeded case

quick_english: If a purified person gives up the body at the end of initiation, he reaches the supreme state. But if the body is given up in the case of seeded initiation, the result fails because karma is absent.
The initiated person must always guard the bond of pledge-conduct. The guru himself should first ask, understand, and carefully examine the candidate.

A disciple may even beg for initiation with nothing more than durva grass and water. Or the disciple may first give to the guru wealth that is his own or that he has obtained by begging.

tokens.grounds: describes the path to that condition

tokens.grounds: names inner practice without outer form

quick_english: For the two of them, firm identification, understood as cause and its bearer, is what liberates. The external does not succeed without the inner, and the inner does not succeed when cut off from the external.

In the wine bath, the foremost practitioner who seeks liberation may become liberated, because wine is of the nature of Śiva and all mantras arise from Śiva.
There is no difference between Śiva and Śakti; the rays arise from Śakti, and wine produces their bliss. Therefore wine is of the nature of Śiva.

quick_english: His will is the supporting pīṭha in which all that moves and does not move is situated. That foremost pīṭha is Kāmarūpa, and from it comes the pair of bindu and nāda.
The nāda-pīṭha is Pūrṇagiri on the right, and on the left is the pīṭha Uḍḍayana. With bindu as the chief, this is the triad of pīṭhas.

tokens.grounds: they call it the eight front petals of the heart-lotus

quick_english: Vārāṇasī, Kāliṅga, Kulūtā, and likewise Lāhulā belong to the eight upakṣetras, which they say correspond to the eight front petals of the heart-lotus.
Viraja and Airuḍikā, Hālā, Elā, Pūḥ, Kṣīrikā, Purī, the place called Māyā, and Marudeśa are understood in both outer and inner form.

Mountain tops, riverbanks, and solitary liṅgas—why say more? All of that is in consciousness and present in prāṇa.

Likewise, even one situated in a sacred seat attains fitness for knowledge, yoga, and the rest, primarily for one who sees inwardly in the body, in the breath, and in consciousness.

This whole universe is already here, so what is the use of other outward displays of wandering? Thus, for those who seek the fruit of each respective circle, the matter applies both inwardly and outwardly.
The difference of sacred places is varied and, in scripture, beyond counting. In the Vīrāvalihṛdaya, seven places are mentioned, along with a pair of śakti-lotuses.

tokens.quick_gloss: when it is about to go there

tokens.quick_gloss: what is in front of that

quick_english: In the procedure of installation, the Lord Śambhu is the deity. How could he be excluded? His limbs also exist and are part of it.

tokens.grounds: joined with the form and limbs

quick_english: The form, emanation, and the three principles, together with the form and limbs, are to be understood as belonging to Shiva with his limbs. The installation is declared to be sixfold.
Above this, one should then perform the sixfold Shakta installation. First comes Parāparā with her faces, and thus Mālinī at the beginning.

tokens.grounds: afterward the triad beginning with Parā
placed at crest, heart, and feet
in the head, face, and throat
from heart, navel, secret place, and thighs

quick_english: After that, the triad beginning with Parā is installed in order at the crest, heart, and feet. Then the sequence continues through the head, face, throat, heart, navel, secret place, and thighs.

tokens.grounds: also in knee and foot, beginning with Aghorā
the fivefold limbs of the vidyā
then one should invoke the Shakti
whose form is the being of the Mother

quick_english: The sequence beginning with Aghorā is placed in the knee and foot. Then come the five limbs of the vidyā. After that, one should invoke the Shakti whose form is the being of the Mother.

tokens.grounds: augmented by the twelve Shaktis of limbs, faces, and retinue

quick_english: One invokes Yogeśvarī, the supreme, full, steadfast Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, augmented by the twelve Shaktis of her limbs, faces, and retinue.

tokens.grounds: according to the difference of aim and practice
in the middle of the triad of goddesses

quick_english: At the time of installation, the guru should contemplate according to the aim and practice of the rite. The supreme goddess, abiding in the middle of the triad, is the non-differentiating one.

tokens.grounds: she, this being of unlimited consciousness alone

quick_english: She is proclaimed as the being of unlimited consciousness alone. This is declared in the Sāra scripture and in the Yāmala, and therefore this is how the goddess is understood.

tokens.grounds: the triad of Shaktis and then the eight

quick_english: The form with faces, the Shakti, the triad of Shaktis, the group of eight, the five limbs, and the supreme Shakti make up the Shakta installation, which is also sixfold.

tokens.grounds: granting the fruits of accomplishment and liberation

quick_english: This Yāmala great installation gives the fruits of accomplishment and liberation. But one who seeks liberation alone should first perform the Shakta installation.

tokens.grounds: which pair of installations has been stated

quick_english: The gurus say that for one who desires liberation, the pair of installations described should be performed beginning with the feet, in the order of withdrawal.

tokens.grounds: denoting Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual

quick_english: However many divisions are declared as denoting Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual, in all those mantras the installation is proclaimed as sixfold.

tokens.grounds: but the one to be invoked
this is stated as sixfold alone

quick_english: But the mantra that is invoked, endowed with its limbs, should be the sixth. Thus in all cases this installation is stated as sixfold.
Afterward come the display of mudrās by body, mind, and speech. There are the five states beginning with waking, and a sixth called the unsurpassed.

tokens.grounds: because of six causes and sixfold selfhood, the joining of the thirty-six principles

quick_english: Because of the six causes, the sixfold selfhood, and the joining of the thirty-six principles, when the sixfold great installation is performed, this whole universe is powerfully brought into unity.

tokens.grounds: beginning from the installation of the form

quick_english: Having attained identity in the body, one should reveal a pure emanation. Beginning from the installation of the form, the emanation that has spread forth here is that pure emanation.

tokens.grounds: by the force and sequence of the installation
regarding the shaking off of the burning of bonds

quick_english: By the power and order of the installation, the emanation is brought to non-difference and made pure. Therefore those deluded people who object regarding the shaking off of the burning of bonds are mistaken.
When one is established in peaceful Shiva, why would he descend again? Those who ask this are refuted from the outset, for they do not understand the ultimate reality of Śambhu.

tokens.grounds: devoid of the essence of the flashing of their own awareness

quick_english: They do not know, because they are devoid of the essence of the flashing of their own awareness. For this peaceful Shiva is not some differentiated entity.

tokens.grounds: describes a limited form like a pot
states the dynamic unfolding of awareness

quick_english: Anything excluded from all other paths is limited somewhere, like a pot. But this consciousness, whose nature is great light, truly expands.
That consciousness is Shiva, and Shiva's nature is to appear as all forms. Therefore, through that very manifestation, he expands by his own essence.

tokens.grounds: refers to what appears in manifestation
states the emergence of the limited subject

quick_english: In this manifestation, both non-difference and difference of one's own self appear. When difference expands, maya unfolds, and with it the maya-bound subject comes into play.

tokens.grounds: the one who can realize Shiva-nature

quick_english: When non-difference expands, that very maya-bound subject unfolds into Shiva-nature. The maya-bound subject attains this through skill gained by practicing identification with that form.

tokens.grounds: emphasizes Shiva as the true agent

quick_english: Shiva alone is declared to be the fruit of that practice, including nyasa and the rest. For just as one becomes shaped by contemplating, 'I am a doer of bad deeds,' so too contemplation determines one's state.

tokens.grounds: shows the effect of this contemplation

quick_english: So too, for one who contemplates, 'I am Shiva, I am no other,' the result follows accordingly. This alone is called firmness: when it has gone to the very heart of reflective awareness.

tokens.grounds: describes the path to the non-conceptual state
the state attained through that path

quick_english: The non-conceptual state is reached through streams of thought centered on identity with Shiva. Otherwise, how could that pure reality, which lives by the very life of reflective awareness, be approached?

tokens.grounds: questions the possibility of such a form
explains how the impossible becomes possible

quick_english: How could any form of that whose nature is to shine ever remain unexamined by awareness? Therefore, by the power of its sovereign free will, this reality accomplishes even what seems most difficult.

tokens.grounds: states the true status of limited faculties

quick_english: Even though breath, intellect, and the like appear to shine, one should not conceive them as having their own independent nature. On the contrary, their nature is opposite to that of the supremely free self.

tokens.grounds: describes the true status of limited faculties
describes the result of wrong certainty

quick_english: If one ascertains these faculties only as perishable and dependent on the Lord, one sinks into a certainty that cuts one off into participation in samsara.

Instead, one should take refuge in a non-conceptual abiding that comes through certainty in the eternal and so forth. But those who are endowed with purity born of the most intense descent of grace are different.

tokens.grounds: negates the need for ritual steps
refers to the highly qualified practitioners
ritual acts they do not require

quick_english: It has been explained that those purified by the most intense grace do not perform initiation and nyasa. But in this way, one who has the universe as his body clearly attains the state of being the universal self.

From nyasa alone, the body becomes transformed in that way, and one should worship it with flowers and other offerings. This may be done in detail with separate mantras, or briefly with the root mantra.

tokens.grounds: repeats the two modes of practice
gives a doctrinal reason for using the left hand

quick_english: With incense, food offerings, acts of satisfaction, and so on, worship may be done in elaborate or concise form. Because samsara moves in a leftward way, all of this should be done with the left hand.
The teacher should also perform the rite of offering with that unimpaired hand. In the revered Matanga and other texts, the word 'left' is said to signify the secret.
The mantra practitioner devoted to left practice should perform the worship; this is stated clearly in the revered Bharga-shikha scripture and likewise in the revered Agama teaching.

tokens.grounds: refers back to the compared merit
states the superior result of the rite

quick_english: Whatever merit there is in all sacred places and whatever fruit there is in all sacrifices, that fruit, O beloved, is multiplied ten million times by offering to the unimpaired one.

tokens.grounds: ritual implement in the cited rule

quick_english: In the revered Nandi-shikha and in the revered Ananda teaching it is said that the ladle should be full, and the spoon should be used in the offering of ghee.

tokens.grounds: describes the resulting state of the body

quick_english: The rest, including worship, fire offering, recitation, and so on, should be done with the left hand alone. In this way the body becomes filled with bliss and free from turning outward toward everything.

tokens.grounds: sets the condition for what remains

quick_english: Having accomplished the body through worship, one should contemplate it as of Shiva-nature. When outward turning toward objects has dissolved and limitation has melted away, this contemplation becomes clear.
When limitation has dissolved, what would remain in the body apart from the essence of Shiva-bliss? The body is filled with the essence of Shiva-bliss and pervaded by the thirty-six principles.

tokens.grounds: the object of vision and worship
states the result of continuous practice

quick_english: Seeing and worshipping the body day and night, one becomes of Shiva-nature. Such a person is satisfied, resting in the body as the universal self and established in its sign.

Such a person does not desire external observances like linga vows, sacred places, and similar practices. The rites were taught so that consciousness might come to rest, and for one in whom it already rests, that is enough.

tokens.grounds: specifies the scope of those rites

quick_english: The higher rites, extending up to external worship, are to be accomplished here for the sake of realizing Shiva-nature. Therefore, the offering vessel should be made as the supreme reality consisting of non-difference from Shiva.

quick_english: As if trembling, those consciousness-senses with cooperators; then in his right hand is shining, all-path-filled.
The guru should worship the bond-burning circle of mantras with the left hand, then place that hand of the disciple on the head of the disciple whose body contains the whole continuum of paths.
He should place in order on all the limbs and touch the disciple with that very hand; this is taught in the Dīkṣottara as done with a hand shining with a cascade of flames.
By the bestowal of the Śiva-hand he is made a samaya-initiate; while still alive he becomes fit for knowledge, and he attains union in the level of Īśvara.
But in the Śrīdevyāthāmala it is taught in a circle with an eight-spoked inner trident, with Bhairava at the navel and Aghora and the other eight forming it.
It is visualized with an outer lower part and a supreme rim, and with a middle trident having supreme and lower aspects, all flame-filled, reddish, and fearsome with whirling Mothers and the praṇava.

tokens.grounds: refers to the circle or hand

quick_english: When this is contemplated and seen in the outer hand, one becomes a samaya-initiate; but if agitation of the bonds and the like appears at once, that shows the person is about to depart.
If he is about to depart, the guru should worship outside that and cast upon the head what separates him from the life-breaths; by this Śiva-hand he clearly becomes a samaya-initiate.
For that same person, in the future proper separation from the bonds of the levels, he has the status of a son, and the initiating teachers are to join him to the supreme level.
That same person, knowing the kinds of mantras and the truth of recitation, fire-offering, and the rest, is consecrated first with the liberation vessel and then with the one called Īśvara.
When consecrated he becomes a sādhaka, and at the end of enjoyment he dissolves into the supreme; endowed with these qualities, one is initiated in the teaching of Śiva.
One who knows the four-part scriptures, is devoted to the eighteen tantras, and knows the ten tantras and the higher path is appointed as an ācārya.
In the consecration rite, the best of gurus should perform for the ācārya the joining that begins from earth and ends in liberation.
By these statements it is said that the samaya-initiate, like a prince, would be authorized everywhere in the three stages beginning with the son stage.
A son-initiate may be authorized in teacherhood if his joining is equal, but he is not authorized in sādhana when the joining is different.
In this tantra, the ācārya is one who has obtained the higher rites through the sequence beginning with samaya; never a Buddhist, Vaiṣṇava, or the like.
Thus what arose by context has been settled, and now the main topic is taken up again: having performed the Śiva-hand rite, by that the disciple's bonds are burned away.
Having brought the disciple, through meditative absorption, to the point of rest, the guru then places that child-disciple in the vessel, in the weapon-vessel, in the fire, and in his own self.
He should have the disciple make prostration, then cast an offering to the beings and Mothers; then, having worshipped Śaṃkara, he should prepare a bed consecrated with the weapon-mantra.
Having placed the disciple on that bed and installed the mantras, the guru establishes rest in the disciple's heart-wheel and then goes to his twelve-end.
Through the arising of the twelve vowels the net of kalās becomes diminished; then, on entry, he becomes bright with the sixteen kalās gathered together.
As the full moon of his own consciousness, he should rest in the heart of the child-disciple until the rising, and then go to the twelve-end.
He should enter the heart-wheel again in this way; this is the sequence of the sleep rite. When sleep has come, this disciple perceives the stainless moon and sun.
In the heart-wheel he forcibly joins together the full and the thin moon and sun, and he truly sees the light of the forcibly stainless moon and sun.
He sees a dream that clearly reveals future good and other outcomes; and it is taught that, having meditated on the full and the thin in the domain of the twelve, this occurs.

Compassion, forbearance, non-envy, purity, good conduct, auspiciousness, non-miserliness, and non-desire are remembered as this eightfold set of qualities of the self.
The girdle, staff, skin, lifelong observances, fire worship, twilight rite, and alms are the seven consecrations, and there are also seven vows.
The Bhauta and Pashupata are two, then the Ganesha and Ganapatya, and with the Unmattaka, sword-edge, and Ghrita-lord observances they make fourteen in all.
These are remembered as the principal consecrations of vow-binding; in the case of renunciation, the final rite is as if in the womb, and by that one is consecrated.

Thus, in sequence, with the head and other limbs, again and again: because the twice-born state is truly of the nature of consciousness, characterized by peace and the rest.
Therefore awareness arises in the state of Rudra through that very sequence, just as gold and other metals, in refining, are transformed by the force of sequence.
Likewise, as with silver and the rest, in the consecration of awareness within the twice-born state the womb is not the cause; there, one who is of peaceful nature is called twice-born.
This has been examined by the sage in the Moksha-dharma and elsewhere, and it has also been ascertained by the Lord in scriptures such as the Mukuta.
Because awareness can arise similarly through similar bodily connection, from the standpoint of common convention, in the Smarta sense the son of two twice-born parents is called twice-born.
Even seers born of mothers associated with low-caste conditions of mind, speech, or birth had elevated minds; what need, then, of brahminhood alone to be a worthy receptacle?
For this reason, in this secret scripture that teaches the truth of real meaning, conduct based on birth and similar factors is indeed taught for the Śāmbhava path.
But the pāśava scriptures are thoroughly of the nature of vāma-śakti, serving accomplishment in creation and related aims, and also serving fear and the arrangement of results under Śambhu.
For one who has been made twice-born, descent from the twelve-end comes not merely by touch, but by resting in union with one's own self and suddenly descending.
By the conferring of a Rudra-share, the samaya-initiate becomes consecrated and is thereby fit for study, hearing, daily worship, and service to the guru.
One authorized as a samaya-initiate should worship the Lord under the guru, and the guru should make that person, now given a Rudra-share, hear the samaya-pledges.
In the Yāmala and related texts of the Goddess, the pledges are set forth as eight groups of eight, including restraint in speech and action, concealment, worship, satiation, and contemplation.
Striking and deluding, and so on, belong to an eightfold set of pledges expressed in eight ways, forming the unified samaya conduct that reflects the nature of mantra and tantra.
One should not speak false, harsh, or untrue words, nor engage in fruitless action, harm, or touching another's wife.
One should not practice pride, hypocrisy, or rites for spirits, poison, and disease, and one should guard one's own mantra, rosary, and knowledge that has the nature of true knowledge.
One should conceal one's conduct, qualities, hardships, and signs of success, and one should honor the guru, the scripture, the god, the fire, elders in knowledge, women, and the vow.
According to one's ability, one should worship the guru-lineage and this eightfold group: the poor, the afflicted, ancestors, field-guardians, living beings, and birds.
One should satiate the cremation-ground host of beings, the goddess of the body, Śiva, Śakti, and likewise the self, as well as the seal that has the form of mantra.
One should contemplate worldly enjoyment and liberation as taught by the guru, and restrain attachment, hatred, envy, contraction, jealousy, and pride.
One should strike down those who break the pledges and their wrong practices, as well as the cruel and hostile followers of the bound path, slanderers, and dullards.
One should delude the king's evil attendants and those who create obstacles, and one should worship the shakinis, who are described in this way in the revered scripture.

In restraints and the like, when one becomes immobile, only a limited state is grasped, like that hardened snow; but from a properly worshipped guru one obtains full, expanding knowledge.
Consciousness is present everywhere and abides in the knowable; the teaching of one who knows this can immediately lift one upward. Therefore one should worship the guru.
